newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds idle, muted by T-note auction.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds idle, muted by T-note auction.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities saw little action on Tuesday as the Treasury's quarterly refunding operation sidelined many traders, market sources said.

"It's been pretty quiet here today in mortgages," said one trader. He said conventionals, those pass-throughs issued to private investors or to Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac, had a "full day" of activity. "Conventionals had a good bid," he added.
The Treasury Department auctioned $17.75 billion in three-year notes Tuesday afternoon, an operation deemed "professional" by several market participants.
"Spreads might widen from here in the short term, but in the intermediate to longer term, I'm very bullish on mortgages," she said.
By late afternoon, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper was off 1/32 at 100-20/32, yielding 105 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were 1/32 lower as well, at 100-15/32 and 100-20/32, respectively.
The 10-year Treasury note was off 1/32 to yield 6.41 percent.
